studies.label: Dynamic online Alternate Uses Task experiment: AI exposure and disclosure
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Assignment is to randomized within-person condition/item sequences, not to randomized clusters. Local-outcome mixed models include participant random intercepts crossed with response chains nested in item-condition combinations (PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1). Global diversity uses permutation tests paired on item and Monte Carlo seed (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1); diversity evolution uses item random intercepts on pooled idea sets (PDF p. 25, SI 8.3). The latter analyses do not supply participant-level uncertainty.

studies.task: Participants ranked supplied examples and wrote one creative use for each everyday object in a randomized condition sequence, with submitted ideas passed to later participants in the same condition-item response chain (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.4.2-3.4.4).

estimates.outcome: Individual creativity: predicted originality of the submitted idea
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Organisciak et al. fine-tuned GPT-3 Davinci classifier predicting human originality ratings normalized to a scale of 1-5; one submitted idea per trial. The paper labels this creativity but measures originality (PDF p. 3, Section 1.2.1; PDF p. 13, Appendix A.1).

stats.difference_is: regression.coef is the adjusted treatment-minus-Control difference in raw originality score.

regression.model: Table 18 linear mixed model: condition (Control reference), self-perceived creativity, relative AI creativity, interest group, response-chain trial number, AI feeling, condition order, log duration, and number of seeds. Participant random intercept crossed with response chains nested within item-condition. No condition-by-moderator interactions retained. Conventional denotes model-based mixed-model SE, not a separately reported sandwich estimator (PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1; PDF p. 21, Table 10).

estimates.outcome: Global idea diversity: median pairwise cosine distance
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: SBERT embeddings; median pairwise cosine distance, multiplied by 100 by the authors. For each condition-item combination, 50 ideas are sampled in each of 50 Monte Carlo runs, using submitted ideas after the sixth trial of a response chain. Contrasts compare means of the resulting set-level diversity values, paired on item and Monte Carlo seed (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1). The exact SBERT checkpoint is not named.

stats.difference_is: As printed in Diff in Means: treatment minus control, in the authors' scaled cosine-distance units.

paper_effect.standardizer: Nonparametric ordering effect across Monte Carlo set-diversity values; no SD standardizer. Positive means larger diversity in the first named condition (PDF p. 21, SI 8.1).

For idea diversity and AI adoption, we scale the dependent variable (cosine distance or cosine similarity, respectively) by 100 for easier interpretation.

sources.quote: For 50 Monte Carlo runs with different seed values, we sampled 50 ideas for each {[condition], item} combination.

estimates.notes: Randomized within-person sequence; no first-round-only contrast is reported. Participants could stop before completing all conditions, and a Control trial could follow an AI trial. Participant counts for this analysis and individual contrasts are not printed; none is inferred from observations or degrees of freedom. The two-tailed permutation test is paired over Monte Carlo seed and item, not independent people; p_value is Holm-Bonferroni adjusted. Total analyzed sets and distinct people underlying this comparison are not printed. Numerical arm levels, arm SDs, arm SEs, difference SEs and confidence limits are not tabulated. Median-diversity arm levels and confidence bars appear only graphically in Figure 7 (PDF p. 7) and are not read off the figure. This is the paper's main global-diversity metric.

estimates.notes: Randomized within-person sequence; no first-round-only contrast is reported. Participants could stop before completing all conditions, and a Control trial could follow an AI trial. Participant counts for this analysis and individual contrasts are not printed; none is inferred from observations or degrees of freedom. This is a slope contrast for collective diversity, not after_ai or an individual moderator analysis. Arm-mean and arm-mean-SE fields remain null. The trial_no coefficient and its SE describe the Control slope and are preserved in resolutions, not relabeled as a mean. The AI-arm slope is not printed and is not computed by adding coefficients. n_units counts pool-level observations across all conditions, not a two-arm count. No participant-level or response-chain-adjusted uncertainty is reported for this pooled analysis. The p-value bound follows the coefficient's significance mark and the printed legend; no exact p-value is computed. Reported robustness metric for diversity evolution.

open_items: The number randomized, per-arm participant counts, complete-pair counts and distinct participant counts for each analysis are not printed. The study-wide analyzed count is not substituted for any unknown analysis count.

No first-round-only comparison is reported. Retained records use the randomized within-person sequence, with incomplete sequences and possible carryover into later Control trials. The paired code describes use of repeated-condition data, not complete pairing or a paired t test.

Individual-originality arm means, participant-level SDs, outcome SDs and standardized treatment effects are not printed. Regression intercepts and coefficient SEs cannot replace arm means or outcome SDs.

Global-diversity arm levels and confidence limits appear only graphically for the main metric. No figure values were read off. Tables 11-13 supply differences, adjusted permutation p-values and Cliff's deltas, but no numerical arm levels or effect SEs and confidence limits.

Global-diversity inference uses Monte Carlo/item pairs; evolution inference uses pooled idea sets with item random intercepts. Neither supplies uncertainty that accounts for the randomized participants.

Table 17 prints Control trial-number slopes and treatment-minus-Control slope differences, but no arm means or numerical AI-arm slopes and their uncertainty. Control slopes and coefficient SEs are preserved in resolutions. Means, mean SEs and unprinted AI slopes are not calculated or substituted.

PDF p. 8, Section 5.2 assigns the positive low-exposure global-diversity result to Undisclosed, whereas PDF p. 22, Table 12 assigns it to Disclosed and gives a negative result for Undisclosed. Extraction follows the explicit table rows; this textual inconsistency remains unresolved.

The abstract says there were no main effects of disclosure, whereas the global-diversity tables print significant disclosure contrasts. Table values are retained without resolving the authors' interpretation.

Full-sample marginal pairwise contrasts are not printed for local idea distance or AI adoption. Condition coefficients in Tables 14 and 22 are conditional on person moderators; centering is not stated. Local distance and AI adoption remain eligible output-based outcomes, but their conditional/moderation results are excluded.

The difference between retained responses in SI 3 and model observation counts is not explained. The observation count for each entire model is recorded as n_units and explicitly distinguished from people and from a two-arm observation count.

The landing page tells everyone examples may come from AI (PDF p. 5, Figure 3). Undisclosed omits source labels, despite the broader description on PDF p. 4 saying participants were not told ideas came from AI.

Table 1 calls AI adoption maximum semantic distance, whereas Sections 1.2.2 and 5.5 and SI 10 define it as maximum cosine similarity. Local idea distance is in SI 8.2, despite Table 1's reference to SI 8.3. The defining sections and model captions determine the outcome descriptions.
The SBERT checkpoint and ChatGPT-3.5 release year are not stated; no release year is inferred from implementation dates. No preregistration was identified in the complete supplied document.
The author version ends mid-sentence in SI 11.3. The supplied citation record identifies a later ACM version of record; that publisher PDF was not used, and content equivalence was not verified.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09 against the supplied PDF and the extraction specification. The complete markdown was read in contiguous chunks through its final line, including all appendices. Every cited PDF page was read with PyMuPDF, and all retained table coefficients, SEs, t statistics, signed global-diversity differences, adjusted p-values and effect sizes were checked against the PDF text. Printed precision is retained in the verbatim source quotations. PDF locators are one-based file pages; the manuscript has no differing printed page numbers. No statistics, counts, arm levels, figure coordinates or new contrasts were calculated. All fields in the supplied difference report and every estimate present only in B have an individual resolution. The inventory retains all four originality contrasts, all ten condition pairs for each global diversity metric, and all four AI-versus-Control slope contrasts for each evolution metric. This includes the global contrasts changing both exposure and disclosure that the screening form omitted. No additional eligible two-arm estimate was found beyond the two extraction inventories. All screening outcomes and contrasts are represented by estimates or by not_extracted. Agreement audit: Table 2 (PDF p. 7) confirms the study count; SI 3 (PDF pp. 17-18) describes response exclusions without a randomized or per-analysis people count. All estimate-level people counts remain null. Table 18 observations are outputs and Table 17 observations are idea pools across the full models, not people or pair-specific counts. Section 1.2.1 (PDF p. 3) establishes originality, giving novelty/with_ai, unit output and higher_is more_creative for S1-O1. SI 8.1 and SI 8.3 (PDF pp. 21 and 25) establish between-person idea-set distances, giving diversity/across_people, unit set and higher_is more_diverse for S1-O3 and S1-O4. Evolution indexes successive participants in a chain, not unassisted work after AI removal, so it is immediate with AI available, not after_ai. Figure 2 and Section 3.4.2 (PDF p. 5) establish randomized within-person order; within_person paired marks the repeated-condition analyses because no first-round estimates are printed. Examples and the idea-entry box share the task screen (PDF p. 16, Figure 12), supporting outcome_with_ai true. Control supplies human examples (PDF p. 2, Figure 1), so AI-versus-Control comparisons are ai_vs_active. For global ai_design pairs, the printed orientation tests Disclosed relative to Undisclosed at fixed exposure and High relative to Low exposure; mixed-factor pairs keep the printed High-minus-Low orientation. Participant random intercepts support se_basis participant for originality (PDF p. 14, Appendix B.1; PDF p. 26, Table 18). The global permutation tests pair on item and Monte Carlo seed, and evolution models account for item but not participant, so both use se_basis set. Model-based SEs are coded conventional; no sandwich estimator is claimed. Statistical significance bounds are transcribed only where coefficient asterisks and the printed legend support them. Matching main-text confidence limits, degrees of freedom and exact p-values are retained for the high-exposure median-diversity slopes, while coefficients and t statistics use the more precise table values. Full-sample eligibility concerns the contrast being estimated, not merely the observations used to fit a model: reference-value person-moderator coefficients and extrapolated trial-zero level coefficients are excluded. Global full-sample level contrasts and response-chain slope differences remain separate outcomes. Control slopes are not arm means. The screening form identifies no other paper sharing S1 participants; historical Organisciak seed ideas and the excluded stimulus benchmark do not share those participants. No preregistration was identified. Only the requested reconciled file is written. Validation: the supplied mechanical checker flags some global-table values because its number matcher permits fewer trailing zeros than the PDF prints. These are formatting false positives; the six-decimal quotations remain verbatim. Independent signed-decimal token checks confirmed every extracted numeric field against its source quotation, and direct PDF row parsing confirmed all retained table values. No source-location, quotation, vocabulary or duplicate-slug problem was reported by the supplied checker. The JSON was reloaded successfully after writing.
